thread:
maria: Morning — StokeBridge go-live window is next Tue 09:00 UTC. Need final signoff on quota + autoscale policy.

anjali: Thanks — confirmed on our side. Main concern is burst traffic from our onboarding batch job (~12k requests/min for ~3m). We need a clear fallback if Dedicated pool can't keep up.

leo: noted. Can you share the batch profile? seq length, avg tokens per request?

anjali: seq avg 160 tokens, 1 request per user, payloads scripted. Peak concurrency map attached (sent privately).

maria: CS ask: quota target 50k tokens/sec sustained, with headroom for 2x bursts. Proposed reserved pool of 4 gpus (A10G), autoscale to 8 for bursts, cooldown 2m.

devon: Ops questions: what latency SLO do they expect? p95 target?

anjali: p95 < 350ms ideally. Some leniency during warmup but want graceful degradation.

leo: p95 350ms with that token rate is tight on A10G if model is large. Suggest quantized variant (q4) for burst path. We can route to q4 when autoscale not caught up.

maria: Proposal summary for StokeBridge:
- Reserved pool: 4 GPUs (region: us-west-2)
- Autoscale max: 8 GPUs, policy: CPU/GPU util trigger 75% for 60s
- Burst routing: fallback to q4 model variant after 20s queue wait
- KV prefix caching enabled for onboarding prompts
- Observability: 1min retention for traces for first 24h

anjali: Sounds good. How do we run a rehearsal load test?

devon: I'll run a stepped soak using k6 from our e2e lab. Plan: 0->12k rps over 6m, hold 3m, then decay. We'll run two passes: warm (no cache) and primed (with cache).

leo: k6 script snippet I'll use to emulate tokens + headers:

```
import http from 'k6/http';
import {sleep} from 'k6';
export let options = {vus: 2000, duration: '15m'}
export default function(){
  http.post('https://api.redwood.example/generate', JSON.stringify({input: '...','max_tokens':160}), {headers: {Authorization: 'Bearer x'}})
  sleep(0.01)
}
```

maria: devon, can you post the exact k6 command and the run window so we can notify StokeBridge?

devon: scheduling for Thu 03:00 UTC (low infra noise). k6 command: `k6 run --vus 2000 --duration 9m stokebridge_load.js` — will capture metrics to grafana. tagging: stokebridge-loadtest-1

deploy-bot: Reserved pool "stokebridge-reserved-usw2" created (4 GPUs). Pool id: rp-7a3b

leo: I'll push the q4 model variant to the pool and wire the routing rule: fallback after 20s queue or error rate > 5%.

maria: Checklist before Thursday: 
- [ ] Confirm IAM/KMS access for customer (maria)
- [ ] Verify users' traffic signature + scripts (anjali)
- [ ] Commit model variants to pool (leo)
- [ ] Configure autoscale policy + cooldowns (devon)
- [ ] Run warm and primed loadtests (devon)

anjali: IAM: confirmed. We'll provide the exact script by EOD tomorrow.

devon: Quick note on autoscale: using 75% GPU util for scale-up, but we'll add a rate-based guard to avoid flapping. Scale-up immediate, scale-down min 3m cooldown. Also enabling prefix cache TTL=30m for onboarding path.

leo: If k6 shows >7% error at p95 we trigger canary fallback to hosted model and throttle non-critical routes. We should pre-authorize that path with StokeBridge.

maria: Can you draft the rollback/fallback runbook snippet? I'll send to StokeBridge ops. Keep it 3 steps.

devon: Draft: 1) Pause incoming onboarding batch (customer trigger). 2) Route subset (20%) to hosted fallback model: `route:set stokebridge -> hosted-llm-v2` 3) Trigger emergency scale (ops) or extend cooldown and open support channel.

anjali: Good — 20% route is acceptable. We'll add a hold script on our side to pause the job if errors spike.

leo: One more: enable token-level cost tags in the first 48h so billing team can reconcile.

maria: Done. I've added billing tag request to the runbook.

devon: Last step: I'll post the grafana dashboard link and the exact k6 run command in #eng-oncall before the test. Expect noise in alerts; we'll mute non-critical paging.

maria: Thanks all — if no objections I'll send the final plan to StokeBridge now. :thumbsup:

anjali: Go ahead, thanks team! :raised_hands:
